quote: My my concern my concern is during the construction, what happened if you you guys damage my roof?
stewart_read: Rep correctly avoids inventing warranty specifics and redirects to the specialist, which is the right scope discipline move rather than a knowledge failure.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply didn't know the warranty terms and dodged. Rejected because the redirect language ('I don't wanna tell you one thing and not have it be that way') shows deliberate discipline, not evasion.
coaching_implication: This is a model example of holding scope — the manager can use this clip to show other reps how to defer without sounding evasive.

quote: Who is it going to cover?
stewart_read: Second time the same liability concern surfaces, and the rep repeats the identical deferral without acknowledging the repetition or reassuring the customer that this is a normal, well-covered scenario.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be intentionally avoiding over-committing on liability language for compliance reasons. Rejected as primary because the rep gives no compliance-based reasoning, just a repeated generic deferral, suggesting under-preparedness rather than a deliberate compliance choice.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to vary the reassurance on a second touch of the same concern — e.g., briefly restating 'that's actually one of the first things the specialist walks through, and it's covered' before deferring, so the customer feels heard rather than looped.

quote: And, you don't do that. It's just on the roof.
stewart_read: Customer is fishing for ground-mount or expanded-array options and net-metering / power-selling programs, an uncatalogued cross-sell/enthusiasm signal not covered by the roofing cross-sell entry in the schema. The rep confirms the roof-only constraint but doesn't flag this as a strong buying signal for the specialist.
coaching_implication: Flag this exchange for the closer brief — customer's appetite for maximizing production (backyard panels, selling power back) is a strong intent signal that should shape how the specialist frames system sizing, even though Ion doesn't offer ground mounts.

quote: And then you sell to the local power company, and then you can make money.
stewart_read: Customer describes a California net-metering model unprompted and says explicitly he's interested in it, a clear buying-motivation signal beyond simple bill reduction.
coaching_implication: Rep should have anchored this explicitly — e.g., 'that overproduction credit is exactly something the specialist will map out for your home' — to convert this enthusiasm into forward pull toward the appointment rather than a generic 'Right.'

quote: And then how long have you been able to call me now? Your company doesn't do it, would you be able to refer me some other company?
stewart_read: Customer directly asks for a referral to another company if Ion doesn't do backyard/ground-mount installs. The rep says 'Okay. Sounds good. Awesome. I'll put that down in the notes here' but never follows up on what specifically he's asking for or confirms this was logged anywhere retrievable by the closer.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may have deliberately moved past this to keep the call on the standard qualification path. Rejected because the customer's request is a concrete unresolved ask that risks being lost entirely if not explicitly carried into a handoff note.
coaching_implication: This unresolved ask should be explicitly captured in the handoff brief so the closer or setter follow-up doesn't leave the customer feeling ignored on a specific request he raised twice.

quote: But you can send me their toll free number or their web so I can go inside. I would prefer phone because, since I don't know my account number and all those types of yeah. I may have difficulty to to get the information from the the web.
stewart_read: Customer signals friction with digital account access, similar to the elderly_low_tech_protocol trigger. Rather than pivoting immediately to a verbal read-back of the paper bill or offering to stay on the line while the customer calls the utility, the rep sends a phone number and defers everything to 'tomorrow,' letting momentum die.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may have judged that keeping the customer on the line while he drives was unsafe or impractical, justifying the deferral. Some support exists since the customer mentions driving at 12:39, but the deferral decision was made at 11:47, before the driving comment, so this doesn't fully explain the miss.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to attempt a verbal kWh read-back or same-call resolution before defaulting to a vague next-day callback — per the schema's 2-minute pivot guidance, the rep let this go past a full minute without offering the readback alternative.

quote: you can just let me know or I can give you a call and then we can set up a meeting. Sure. Does that work?
stewart_read: This is the closest the call gets to a button-up, but it locks nothing — no day, no time, no hour-block, no computer/no-driving instruction. The 'does that work' handshake happens on a plan with zero specificity.
coaching_implication: The manager should flag that this call never reaches a real button-up. Coach the rep to convert 'we'll touch base tomorrow' into a specific window ('I'll call you tomorrow at 10am once you've had a chance to call the utility') even when the bill isn't in hand yet.
